reasons.correctness_risk: The core flows work: duplicate request IDs are ignored, the preview is re-run before commit, the task loop is guarded by runId, and a restart recovers. But proposals are never checked against a field schema or type. A failed reply blocks new messages until it is retried, and a write failure mid-reply leaves the reply stuck pending. Focus is restored by accessible name, so it can land on another proposal's Confirm button.
reasons.structure: records.js and store.js are small and focused. workspace.js is one large closure that holds cookie signing, the reply pipeline, the task runner and every action in a single switch.
reasons.readability: Plain names and straight-line control flow are easy to follow end to end. Only a few crowded Object.assign one-liners and the 'shortcut' name for saved tasks get in the way.
reasons.error_handling: Request checks are good: Host and Origin checks, JSON and size limits, length checks, and 401/404/409 responses. But the snapshot is parsed without validation, so a damaged file crashes startup with a raw exception. Listen errors are unhandled, unexpected errors become an unlogged 500, and proposed values are not type-checked.
reasons.tests: Eight end-to-end scenarios cover setup, identity, saved instructions and tasks, memory, previews, concurrent confirms, tasks (steer, fail, cancel, restart) and the page's accessible names. There are no direct module tests and no fault-injection or damaged-state cases. Restarts happen only inside the test process, and one assertion waits a fixed 800 ms.

reasons.correctness_risk: Very defensive. Previews are checked against a typed schema, amounts must match exactly, and confirms apply all changes or none. Submission receipts survive a reload, run numbers guard task controls, and restart recovery is tested. The risk is its complexity. The 'what is the X of Y' pre-parser also misfires on ordinary questions (e.g. 'of my order'): it withholds the records and shows a notice asking for a record ID.
reasons.structure: Clear split into store, records, tasks and workspace modules, driven by a Chat class, with a thin server. Held back by a large act() switch and by natural-language request parsing living inside the records module.
reasons.readability: Dense and terse. Validator names are cryptic (key, count, rows, fact), and the module binding workspaces is shadowed. Index arithmetic rewrites the user's message for the stand-in, and the conversation-label code is intricate. The client is driven by a dozen module-level flags, with few comments.
reasons.error_handling: Thorough. It checks origin, fetch-site, content type and size, and enforces length limits. Snapshots are validated and never overwritten, symlinks are refused, writes are atomic with a directory fsync, a storage-unavailable mode is reported clearly, and startup errors are friendly. But there is no Host check against DNS rebinding, and any background exception is treated as a storage failure that disables the whole app.
reasons.tests: Three suites pin both the module rules and end-to-end behaviour. They include real process restarts, injected file-system faults, concurrent confirmations, idempotent receipts, stale controls, privacy and boundary inputs. The gaps are short polling windows and no check of the page's accessible names.

why: Y is much more defensive and better tested. It checks proposals against a schema, keeps submissions idempotent across reloads, ignores stale task controls and validates and atomically saves its state, with module-level, fault-injection and real-restart tests behind it. X is simpler and easier to read, but it leaves record updates untyped, blocks a conversation after a failed reply, crashes on damaged state and tests less deeply, while Y's cost is density and over-engineering, including a lookup heuristic that can misfire on ordinary questions.
